definition_zh: 情节；小块土地；密谋；绘制；标出
definition_en: the arranged sequence of events in a story; a small measured piece of land; a secret plan made by a group; and to mark a course or a set of data on a map or graph
core_image: 田埂围出一小块地，旁边有人低头在纸上描出一条曲线
scene: 剧本读到一半，作者在页边画出一个方框，把人物下一步的动作圈了进去。 She sketched the plot of her next novel on the back of an envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 plot 是「情节」（第 1 个义项：故事中事件的安排）；句意为她在信封背面勾勒出下一部小说的情节。图中可辨识物件：剧本、页边方框、信封。

derivatives.zh: 由 plot 双写末尾的 t 加表示「人或工具」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「密谋者；绘图仪」
由 plot 加 -ing 构成，义为「密谋；绘图」
由前缀 sub-（在下、次要）加 plot 构成，义为「次要情节」

senses.title: The sequence of events in a story
senses.definition: the organized sequence of events and actions that makes up a story, play or film
senses.definitionCN: 构成小说、戏剧或电影的故事事件与行动的有序安排
senses.example: The plot turns on a letter that never arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 情节的关键是一封始终没有送达的信。
senses.why: Plot first named a piece of ground marked off by boundaries, and a story line is likewise a stretch staked out by the writer: a beginning, a turn and an end. The sense is recorded from the seventeenth century, when critics needed a word for the arrangement of incidents in a play.
senses.whyCN: plot 最初指用界线围出的一块地，而故事线同样是一段由作者圈定的范围：开端、转折与结局。这个义项在十七世纪有记录，当时评论家需要一个词来指戏剧中事件的安排。

senses.title: A small measured piece of land
senses.definition: a small area of ground marked out for a particular use, such as building a house or growing vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途（如盖房或种菜）而划出的一小块土地
senses.example: They grow beans on a narrow plot behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋后一小块窄地上种豆子。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded sense: Old English plot named a definite piece of ground, most likely because the patch had been marked off from the rest. The measuring of land by lines is still visible in a garden plot or a building plot.
senses.whyCN: 这是有记录的最古老义项：古英语 plot 指一块界限明确的地，很可能因为这片地被从周围划了出来。用线划分土地的动作至今仍看得见，比如菜地或建筑用地。

senses.title: A secret plan made by several people
senses.definition: a secret plan by a group to do something harmful or unlawful
senses.definitionCN: 一群人暗中策划做有害或违法之事的计划
senses.example: The police uncovered a plot to rob the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 警方破获了一起抢劫银行的阴谋。
senses.why: English speakers blended the native land word with Old French complot, a group scheme; the two forms merged in sound and meaning, so the idea of a secret scheme attached itself to plot and has stayed ever since.
senses.whyCN: 说英语的人把本土表示土地的那个词与古法语 complot（一伙人的图谋）混同，两个形式在读音和意义上合流，于是「暗中图谋」的意思就附着在 plot 上，一直留到今天。

senses.title: To mark a course or data on a graph
senses.definition: to mark points, a line or a course on a map or graph, or to follow and record a moving path
senses.definitionCN: 在地图或图表上标出点、线或路线，或跟踪记录一条移动的轨迹
senses.example: The software plots the temperature against the hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件把温度随时间的变化绘成曲线。
senses.why: Marking points on a sheet repeats on paper the old act of marking ground. Sailors plotted a course by laying it out point by point, and the same verb now covers data points drawn on a graph.
senses.whyCN: 在纸上标出各个点，等于把当年在土地上做记号的动作重做一遍。水手靠逐点标出来绘制航线，同一个动词如今也用于把数据点画成图表。

intro.en: Plot is an old English word for a piece of ground whose earlier origin is uncertain; the sense of a secret scheme came from French complot, and the story sense grew out of the marked-out ground.
intro.cn: plot 是英语中表示一块土地的古老词，更早的来源不确定；「阴谋」的意思来自法语 complot，而「情节」的意思则从划出来的那块地引申而来。

items.en: Old English plot named a definite piece of ground, and its earlier origin is uncertain; it may have meant a patch marked off from the rest.
items.cn: 古英语 plot 指一块界限明确的地，更早的来源不确定，可能指从周围划出来的一小片。

items.en: Middle English used plot for a small field or a measured patch, and the word stayed close to land and boundaries.
items.cn: 中古英语用 plot 指小田地或量好的一小块地，词义始终离不开土地与界线。

items.en: Old French complot meant a group scheme or conspiracy; English speakers heard it as the same word as plot and merged the two meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 complot 指一伙人的图谋或阴谋；说英语的人把它听成与 plot 同一个词，两种意思便合在一起。

items.en: In the sixteenth century plot could mean a secret plan, and by the seventeenth critics used it for the arranged incidents of a play.
items.cn: 十六世纪时 plot 已可指秘密计划，到十七世纪评论家又用它指戏剧中安排好的事件。

items.en: Modern English keeps the land, the scheme and the story, and adds the verb of charting a course or plotting data.
items.cn: 现代英语保留土地、阴谋与故事三层意思，又加上绘制航线或标绘数据的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers this word's own family plus the French cousin behind the conspiratorial sense; the near-meaning group gathers words for a story line, a scheme and a patch of ground.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及带来「阴谋」义的那个法语近亲；近义组收表示故事线、图谋与小块地的词。

normalIntro.en: The word began as ground marked off by lines, and that single picture of a bounded patch keeps reappearing: a patch of soil, a stretch of events, a set of points on a sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从被线条划出的土地开始，而「一块有边界的范围」这个画面反复出现：一块土、一段事件、纸上一组点。

normal.en: Old English plot meant a measured piece of ground, so the garden plot and the building plot are the oldest uses of the word.
normal.cn: 古英语 plot 指量好的一块地，所以菜地与建筑用地是这个词最古老的用法。

normal.en: A story plot is a stretch of events with a boundary: the writer decides where the tale starts and where it stops.
normal.cn: 故事的情节是一段有边界的事件：作者决定故事从哪里开始、到哪里结束。

normal.en: The conspiratorial sense came from French complot, which English speakers heard as the same word and merged with plot.
normal.cn: 阴谋义来自法语 complot，说英语的人把它听成同一个词，于是与 plot 合并。

normal.en: To plot a graph is to mark points one by one, the way a surveyor marks a patch of ground.
normal.cn: plot 一张图就是逐个标出点，正如测量员标出一块地。

normal.en: Subplot adds sub-, meaning under or secondary, so it names a story line running beneath the main one.
normal.cn: subplot 加了表示「在下、次要」的 sub-，指主线之下的一条情节。

abstract.en: A plot is a line drawn around a piece of the world so that attention can settle there.
abstract.cn: 情节是围绕世界的一小块画出的线，好让注意力落在那里。

abstract.en: The same word holds a garden and a conspiracy, because both are marked out in advance by someone who intends to use them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既装着菜地也装着阴谋，因为两者都是有人事先划出来、打算加以利用的。

abstract.en: On a graph, a plot is a promise that a movement can be turned into a shape.
abstract.cn: 在图表上，一条绘出的曲线是一个承诺：一段运动可以被变成形状。

senses.title: Proof in a case
senses.definition: facts that help prove something
senses.definitionCN: 帮助证明某事的事实
senses.example: The police collected evidence at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在现场收集证据。
senses.why: Evidence is what makes a claim visible and clear.
senses.whyCN: 证据让主张变得可见而清楚。

senses.title: A sign
senses.definition: a sign that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 表明某事属实的迹象
senses.example: There is evidence of rain in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山里有下雨的迹象。
senses.why: The word extends from courts to ordinary observation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法庭延伸到日常观察。

senses.title: To show
senses.definition: to show or prove something
senses.definitionCN: 表明或证明某事
senses.example: The results evidence a clear improvement.
senses.exampleCN: 结果显示出明显的改善。
senses.why: The noun also became a formal verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也变成了正式动词。

intro.en: Evidence comes from Latin evidentia, clearness, from evidens, clearly seen.
intro.cn: evidence 源自拉丁语 evidentia（清楚），来自 evidens（清楚可见的）。

items.en: Videre means to see.
items.cn: videre 意为看。

items.en: Evidens means clearly seen.
items.cn: evidens 意为清楚可见的。

items.en: Evidentia means clearness.
items.cn: evidentia 意为清楚。

items.en: French evidence carries the sense of proof.
items.cn: 法语 evidence 带有证明的含义。

items.en: Evidence names facts that prove something.
items.cn: evidence 指能证明某事的事实。

note.en: Evidence supports a claim; proof settles it.
note.cn: evidence 支持一个主张；proof 则能定论。

entries.definition: clear and obvious
clearly
relating to evidence
facts that settle a question
something that shows a fact
a statement given in court

normalIntro.en: Evidence is truth laid out where everyone can see it.
normalIntro.cn: evidence 是摆出来让所有人看见的事实。

normal.en: Clear evidence leaves little doubt.
normal.cn: 明确的证据让人几乎无从怀疑。

normal.en: Evidence of rain means signs that rain fell.
normal.cn: evidence of rain 意为下过雨的迹象。

normal.en: Give evidence means tell what you know in court.
normal.cn: give evidence 意为在法庭上作证。

normal.en: Scientific evidence comes from careful tests.
normal.cn: 科学证据来自严谨的实验。

normal.en: Compare proof: evidence supports, proof settles.
normal.cn: 对比 proof：evidence 支持，proof 定论。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass over a single fingerprint.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜对准一枚指纹。

abstract.en: Imagine small marks that tell a whole story.
abstract.cn: 想象一些细小痕迹讲出完整故事。

abstract.en: Think of a light that makes a hidden fact visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一束让隐藏事实显形的光。

examples.en: The evidence supports her story.
examples.cn: 证据支持她的说法。

examples.en: Scientists found evidence of water on the planet.
examples.cn: 科学家在这颗行星上发现了水的证据。

examples.en: He gave evidence in court.
examples.cn: 他在法庭上作证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ vidence（看）」——把事实摆出来让人看见，就是证据。

root: 拉丁语 evidentia（清楚可见）← evidens（显露的）← e-（出）＋ videre（看）→ evidence。

sensesIntro.en: Evidence begins as proof in a case, extends to any sign, and then becomes a formal verb meaning to show.
sensesIntro.cn: evidence 先指案件中的证据，再指任何迹象，最后作正式动词表示表明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnifying glass, photos and papers on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的放大镜、照片与文件。

branches.en: Proof in a case is the core sense.
branches.cn: 案件中的证据是核心含义。

branches.en: Any sign can count as evidence.
branches.cn: 任何迹象都可算作证据。

branches.en: The verb means to show clearly.
branches.cn: 动词意为清楚地表明。

branches.en: Courts and daily life both read signs.
branches.cn: 法庭与日常生活都在解读迹象。

branches.en: The noun and verb share one act of showing.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共用一个展示行为。

intro.en: Evidence comes from the Latin root vid, to see.
intro.cn: evidence 来自拉丁词根 vid（看）。

latinIntro.en: Latin evidentia gives the word its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evidentia 赋予这个词形态。

items.exampleCN: evidens 由 e- 与 videre 组成。
evident 描述清楚明显的事物。

definition_en: strong belief in a religion; firm trust in someone or something; a religion; loyalty and honesty in a relationship or promise
core_image: 在看不见终点时仍把手交给对方
scene: 我对她的判断有信心。 I have faith in her judgement.
sceneCN: 这里 faith 是「信心、信任」（第 2 个义项）；句意：我对她的判断有信心。

senses.title: Religious belief
senses.definition: strong belief in a religion or in God
senses.definitionCN: 对宗教或上帝的坚定信仰
senses.example: Her faith gave her strength.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信仰给了她力量。
senses.why: The core sense is trust in what cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是对不可见之物的信任。

senses.title: Firm trust
senses.definition: firm trust in a person, plan, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、计划或想法的坚定信任
senses.example: We have faith in the new manager.
senses.exampleCN: 我们对新经理有信心。
senses.why: Religious trust extends to everyday confidence.
senses.whyCN: 宗教信任延伸到日常的信心。

senses.title: A religion
senses.definition: a particular religion or system of belief
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定宗教或信仰体系
senses.example: People of many faiths live here.
senses.exampleCN: 许多不同信仰的人住在这里。
senses.why: The belief becomes a named community.
senses.whyCN: 信仰变成有名号的群体。

senses.title: Loyalty
senses.definition: loyalty and honesty in a relationship or promise
senses.definitionCN: 在关系或承诺中的忠诚与诚实
senses.example: He kept faith with his old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他对老朋友信守情义。
senses.why: Trust between people becomes a bond of honour.
senses.whyCN: 人与人之间的信任成为信义纽带。

intro.en: Faith comes from Old French feid, from Latin fides, trust.
intro.cn: faith 来自古法语 feid，源头是拉丁语 fides（信任）。

items.en: Fides means trust or faithfulness.
items.cn: fides 意为信任或忠诚。

items.en: Fidere means to trust.
items.cn: fidere 意为信任。

items.en: Feid carries the sense of loyalty.
items.cn: feid 带有忠诚之义。

items.en: Faith means belief and promise.
items.cn: 中古英语中 faith 兼指信念与承诺。

items.en: Faith covers religion and personal trust.
items.cn: 现代英语中 faith 涵盖宗教与个人信任。

note.en: Faith is trust; fate is destiny.
note.cn: faith 是信任，fate 则是命运。

entries.definition: weak or unclear
the power that decides events
just and equal
the feeling that something is true
firm belief in someone's honesty
a system of worship and belief

normalIntro.en: Faith is trust that holds even when proof is missing.
normalIntro.cn: faith 是在缺少证据时仍然坚持的信任。

normal.en: She never lost faith in her team.
normal.cn: 她从未对团队失去信心。

normal.en: They acted in good faith.
normal.cn: 他们出于善意行事。

normal.en: People of different faiths prayed together.
normal.cn: 不同信仰的人一起祈祷。

normal.en: He kept faith with his promise.
normal.cn: 他信守承诺。

normal.en: It was an act of faith to start the business.
normal.cn: 创办这家企业是一种信念之举。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching out in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中伸出的手。

abstract.en: Imagine a promise kept without witnesses.
abstract.cn: 想象没有见证人时仍守住的承诺。

abstract.en: Think of a light you trust before you see it.
abstract.cn: 把信仰想成一盏尚未看见却相信的灯。

examples.en: Her faith in people remained strong.
examples.cn: 她对人的信心依然坚定。

examples.en: The treaty was signed in good faith.
examples.cn: 条约是本着善意签署的。

examples.en: Patients need faith in their doctor.
examples.cn: 病人需要信任自己的医生。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: faith 与 fidelity、confide 同源于拉丁语 fides（信任），核心就是「信」。

root: faith 经由古法语 feid 来自拉丁语 fides（信任、忠诚），与 fidelity、confide 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Faith is religious belief, firm trust, a religion, or loyalty.
sensesIntro.cn: faith 指宗教信仰、坚定信任、某宗教，或忠诚信义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: trust offered without visible proof.
core.cn: 核心意象：在看不见证据时给予的信任。

branches.en: The base sense is trust in the unseen.
branches.cn: 基础义是对不可见之物的信任。

branches.en: Trust extends to people and plans.
branches.cn: 信任延伸到人与计划。

branches.en: The belief becomes a named religion.
branches.cn: 信仰变成有名号的宗教。

branches.en: Trust between people becomes loyalty.
branches.cn: 人与人之间的信任成为忠诚。

branches.en: Religious faith and personal honour both keep promises.
branches.cn: 宗教信仰与个人信义都守承诺。

intro.en: Faith builds faithful, faithfully, and faithless.
intro.cn: faith 构成 faithful、faithfully 与 faithless。

latinIntro.en: Latin fides and fidere explain faith and its Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fides 与 fidere 解释了 faith 及其拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: 这座城市欢迎所有宗教。

items.example: He was faithless to his word.
The claim was made in bad faith.
We must keep faith with voters.

latinEntries.example: Fides is the root of faith.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fides 是 faith 的词根。
fidere 是 confide 的前身。

definition_en: the popular style of clothes or behaviour at a time, a particular design, or a way of doing something
core_image: 时装秀的灯光下，模特走过长台，观众记录最新款式
scene: 她的裙子紧跟最新时尚。 Her dress follows the latest fashion.
sceneCN: 这里 fashion 是「时尚」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她的裙子紧跟最新时尚。

senses.title: The prevailing style
senses.definition: the popular style of clothes, behaviour, or decoration at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期流行的服装、行为或装饰风格
senses.example: Short jackets are in fashion this year.
senses.exampleCN: 短夹克今年很流行。
senses.why: The central sense is a shared current style.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是当下被共同追随的风格。

senses.title: A style of clothing
senses.definition: a particular design or make of clothes
senses.definitionCN: 服装的某种设计或样式
senses.example: The dress is available in three fashions.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子有三种款式。
senses.why: The general style narrows to one garment design.
senses.whyCN: 总体风格缩小到某种服装设计。

senses.title: A way of doing something
senses.definition: a particular manner or method
senses.definitionCN: 某种特定的方式或方法
senses.example: He arranged the books in his own fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 他按自己的方式整理书籍。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a manner or way.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是方式或方法。

intro.en: Fashion comes from Latin facere, to make, through Old French façon, a making or manner.
intro.cn: fashion 源自拉丁语 facere（做），经古法语 façon（做法、样式）进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do.
items.cn: facere 意为做或制造。

items.en: Façon meant a making, a shape, or a manner.
items.cn: façon 意为制作、形状或方式。

items.en: Fashion meant a shape or a way of doing something.
items.cn: fashion 意为形状或做事的方式。

items.en: Fashion came to mean the current style of dress.
items.cn: fashion 开始指当下流行的服装风格。

items.en: Fashion covers clothing trends and any popular style.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fashion 涵盖服装潮流与各种流行风格。

note.en: Fashion is compared with similar-looking words and with words for style and trend.
note.cn: 把 fashion 与形近词以及表示风格和潮流的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small group within a larger one
a soft pad to sit or rest on
stylish at a particular time
a distinctive way of doing or making
a general direction of change
a period of popularity

normalIntro.en: Fashion is the noun, fashionable is the adjective, and fashionably is the adverb.
normalIntro.cn: fashion 是名词，fashionable 是形容词，fashionably 是副词。

normal.en: In fashion means popular now.
normal.cn: in fashion 意为当下流行。

normal.en: A fashion show displays new clothes.
normal.cn: fashion show 展示新服装。

normal.en: Fashion and fashionable share the same base.
normal.cn: fashion 与 fashionable 同根。

normal.en: The ion ending often marks a noun.
normal.cn: ion 结尾常提示这是名词。

normal.en: Fashion can mean a way, not only clothes.
normal.cn: fashion 不只指衣服，也可指方式。

abstract.en: Fashion begins as a way of making, and becomes a way of looking.
abstract.cn: fashion 起初是制作方式，后来变成外观方式。

abstract.en: A style becomes fashion only when a group chooses it.
abstract.cn: 样式只有被群体选择后才成为时尚。

abstract.en: Trends change, but the act of following them does not.
abstract.cn: 潮流会变，但追随潮流这件事不会变。

examples.en: Short jackets are in fashion this year.
examples.cn: 短夹克今年很流行。

examples.en: She works in the fashion industry.
examples.cn: 她在时尚行业工作。

examples.en: He arranged the books in his own fashion.
examples.cn: 他按自己的方式整理书籍。

dict_mnemonic.text: fashion 源自拉丁语 facere（做），经法语 façon（做法、样式）而来，从「制作方式」演变为「时尚款式」。

root: 源自拉丁语 facere（做、制造），经古法语 façon（做法、样式），核心义「做出来的样子」。

sensesIntro.en: Fashion means the current popular style, a particular clothing design, or a manner of doing something.
sensesIntro.cn: fashion 意为当下流行风格、某种服装款式，或做事的方式。

core.en: A style that a group chooses and follows.
core.cn: 被一群人共同选择并追随的样式。

branches.en: The style most people follow.
branches.cn: 多数人追随的风格。

branches.en: A particular design of clothing.
branches.cn: 某种特定的服装设计。

branches.en: A personal manner of acting.
branches.cn: 个人做事的方式。

branches.en: Trends and garments reinforce each other.
branches.cn: 潮流与服装互相强化。

branches.en: Both are patterns people adopt.
branches.cn: 两者都是人们采纳的模式。

intro.en: Fashion has a family of adjectives, adverbs, and compounds.
intro.cn: fashion 拥有形容词、副词与复合词构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, to make, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere（做）是远源。

items.exampleCN: 这件外套现在显得过时。
这位时尚达人认识每位设计师。

items.example: The fashion show starts at eight.
The fashion designer won a prize.
items.exampleCN: 这位时装设计师获了奖。

definition_en: on the other side of something, or more than a limit
core_image: 越过山脊后展开的陌生平原
scene: 翻过山脊，眼前展开一片陌生平原。 The village lies beyond the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 beyond 是「在……那边」（第 1 个义项：位于某物的另一侧）；句意是村庄在山的那一边。

derivatives.zh: 语义关联词，义为「超过」，对应 beyond 的越界含义
语义关联词，义为「胜过」，对应 go beyond 的含义

senses.title: On the other side
senses.definition: on the far side of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的另一侧
senses.example: The village lies beyond the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 村庄在山的那一边。
senses.why: This is the oldest spatial sense, looking past a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的空间义，视线越过一条界线。

senses.title: More than a limit
senses.definition: greater than a limit or ability
senses.definitionCN: 超过某个限度或能力
senses.example: The price is beyond our budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这个价格超出了我们的预算。
senses.why: Crossing a physical line became crossing any limit.
senses.whyCN: 越过实际的界线，引申为越过任何限度。

senses.title: Later than a point in time
senses.definition: later than a stated time
senses.definitionCN: 晚于某个时间点
senses.example: Do not stay out beyond ten.
senses.exampleCN: 十点以后别待在外面。
senses.why: Time was treated as a line that can be crossed.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作一条可以越过的线。

intro.en: Beyond is be- plus yond, an old word for the far side.
intro.cn: beyond 是 be- 加上 yond，后者是表示「那边」的古词。

items.en: begeondan meant on the far side.
items.cn: begeondan 意为「在另一边」。

items.en: beyond became the usual form.
items.cn: beyond 成为通用形式。

items.en: the word also meant more than.
items.cn: 这个词也开始表示「超过」。

items.en: beyond belief entered common speech.
items.cn: beyond belief 进入日常表达。

items.en: beyond covers space, limits and time.
items.cn: 如今 beyond 涵盖空间、限度与时间。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- opening; the near-meaning group gives words for passing a point.
note.cn: 形近组都以 be- 开头；近义组是表示越过某点的词。

entries.definition: at the back of something
in a lower position
next to something
further than a point
across or above
at a higher level than

normalIntro.en: Beyond means on the far side, past a line you can see.
normalIntro.cn: beyond 指在可见界线的另一侧。

normal.en: Beyond the hills means on the far side.
normal.cn: beyond the hills 指山的另一边。

normal.en: Beyond belief means too strange to accept.
normal.cn: beyond belief 指难以置信。

normal.en: Beyond control means no one can stop it.
normal.cn: beyond control 指无法控制。

normal.en: Beyond doubt means certainly true.
normal.cn: beyond doubt 指毫无疑问。

normal.en: The word is fixed in form.
normal.cn: 这个词形式固定。

abstract.en: See a ridge with open land past it.
abstract.cn: 想象山脊之后开阔的土地。

abstract.en: See a price tag above a budget line.
abstract.cn: 想象价签高过预算线。

abstract.en: See a clock passing ten at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里时钟越过十点。

examples.en: The village lies beyond the hills.
examples.cn: 村庄在山的那一边。

examples.en: The price is beyond our budget.
examples.cn: 这个价格超出了我们的预算。

examples.en: Do not stay out beyond ten.
examples.cn: 十点以后别待在外面。

dict_mnemonic.text: be 加 yond（那边），站在那边之外，就是 beyond。

root: 古英语 begeondan 由 be- 与 geond（越过）构成，本义「在较远的一边」，中古英语定型为 beyond，后引申为超出限度与迟于某时。

sensesIntro.en: Space, limit and time each have a line that beyond crosses.
sensesIntro.cn: 空间、限度与时间，各自都有一条被 beyond 越过的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ridge with open land past it.
core.cn: 核心意象：山脊之后开阔的土地。

branches.en: beyond the hills
branches.cn: 在山那边

branches.en: beyond the river
branches.cn: 在河那边

branches.en: beyond belief
branches.cn: 难以置信

branches.en: beyond control
branches.cn: 无法控制

branches.en: beyond ten
branches.cn: 十点以后

intro.en: Beyond is a fixed form that takes no endings.
intro.cn: beyond 形式固定，不加词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古英语。

definition_en: to take goods or letters to a place; to give a speech; to do what was promised
core_image: 一双手把包裹递到门口，收件人签下名字
scene: 快递员在午前按响门铃，把纸箱放在门垫上。 The driver delivered the parcel before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 deliver 指「递送」（第 1 个义项：把物品送到某处）；句意是司机在中午前把包裹送到了。

senses.title: Take something to its place
senses.definition: to carry goods, letters or food to the person or place waiting for them
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、信件或食物送到等待的人或地点
senses.example: The driver delivered the parcel before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在中午前把包裹送到了。
senses.why: A thing only counts as sent when it has arrived.
senses.whyCN: 东西只有到了，才算真的寄出去。

senses.title: Give a speech aloud
senses.definition: to speak words to an audience in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式场合向听众讲出一段话
senses.example: She delivered a short speech at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口作了一个简短的讲话。
senses.why: Words too are carried from one mouth to many ears.
senses.whyCN: 话也是被从一个嘴里送到许多只耳朵里的。

senses.title: Do what was promised
senses.definition: to produce the result that was promised or expected
senses.definitionCN: 交出所承诺或所期待的结果
senses.example: The new team delivered results in the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 新团队在第一个月就交出了成果。
senses.why: A promise is only a parcel that has not arrived yet.
senses.whyCN: 承诺不过是一个还没送到的包裹。

intro.en: Deliver comes from Old French delivrer, from Latin de- and liberare, to set free.
intro.cn: deliver 来自古法语 delivrer，底层是拉丁语的 de- 与 liberare（使自由）。

items.en: Liberare meant to set a person free.
items.cn: liberare 意为把人释放、使之自由。

items.en: Delivrer added the sense of handing something over.
items.cn: delivrer 又添上「把东西交出去」的意思。

items.en: English used deliver for freeing and for giving up a thing.
items.cn: 英语用它既表示解救，也表示交出东西。

items.en: The sense of carrying goods to a place grew strong.
items.cn: 把货物送到某地的意思渐渐占了上风。

items.en: One can now deliver a parcel, a speech or a result.
items.cn: 如今可以送包裹、作演讲，也可以交出成果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the liver stem, and the meaning group moves from handing over to sending.
note.cn: 形近组共用 liver 这个词干，近义组则从交给一路走到送出。

a result that must be handed over

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门口的一声铃开始，落到一个终于变成结果的承诺。

normal.cn: 车里的包裹，还只是一个计划。

normal.en: The last step of any journey is a pair of hands.

normal.en: A speech is carried across the room by breath.
normal.cn: 演讲是靠一口气送到屋子对面的。

normal.en: Results are promises that have arrived.
normal.cn: 成果，就是已经送到的承诺。

normal.en: Deliver once meant to set free; now it means to hand over.

examples.en: The driver delivered the parcel before noon.
examples.cn: 司机在中午前把包裹送到了。

examples.en: She delivered a short speech at the door.

examples.en: The new team delivered results in the first month.
examples.cn: 新团队在第一个月就交出了成果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deliver 记成「递礼物」：de 开头，liver 听着像「礼物」，把礼物递到手上，就是送达。

root: 来自古法语 delivrer，底层是拉丁语 liberare（使自由），所以它最早表示「解救、释放」。后来「把东西放出去」变成「把东西交出去」，十五世纪起「送到某地」成为主要意思，又引申出发表演讲与兑现成果。

sensesIntro.en: From a parcel at the door, to words crossing a room, to a promise turned into fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 从门口的包裹，到穿过屋子的话，再到变成事实的承诺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands passing a parcel into other hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手把包裹交到另一双手里。

branches.en: The first sense is a parcel arriving where it was sent.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是包裹到达它被寄去的地方。

branches.en: The second sense carries words instead of goods.
branches.cn: 第二个义项送的是话，不是货。

branches.en: The third sense carries a result that was owed.
branches.cn: 第三个义项送的是欠着的成果。

branches.en: A parcel and a promise both count only when they arrive.
branches.cn: 包裹与承诺，都要到了才算数。

branches.en: Both senses turn something held back into something handed over.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把攥着的东西变成交出去的东西。

intro.en: Deliver has a family of nouns for the act and the person, and an adjective for what never arrived.
intro.cn: deliver 有表示行为与人的名词，也有表示没送到的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is liberare, to free, with de- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 liberare（使自由），前缀 de- 表示离开。

definition_zh: 不寻常的；罕见的；与众不同的；特别的
definition_en: not common or ordinary, and therefore noticed
core_image: 一群灰鸽子中间落着一只白鸽
scene: 小镇的集市上忽然来了个戴高帽的卖艺人，围观的人越聚越多。 It is unusual to see a crowd like this on a weekday.
sceneCN: 这里 unusual 是「不寻常的」（第 1 个义项：很少见、不是常态）；句意为工作日见到这么多人实在少见。灰鸽群中落着一只白鸽，正是这个词的核心。

collocations.phrase: for some reason unusual to us
collocations.zh: 对我们来说不同寻常的原因

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「异常地；格外地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不寻常；罕见」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「通常的」
同源名词，义为「习惯；使用」，派生路径见词源

senses.title: Not happening in the ordinary course
senses.definition: not happening as it normally does
senses.definitionCN: 没有按平常的情形发生
senses.example: It is unusual to find the library this empty.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆空成这样实属少见。
senses.why: The prefix says not and the base says customary, because usual comes from use, a habit.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「不」，词根意为「惯常的」，因为 usual 源自 use（习惯）。

senses.title: Rare enough to be noticed
senses.definition: rare enough that people stop and look
senses.definitionCN: 罕见得让人停下来多看几眼
senses.example: An unusual bird landed on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 一只少见的鸟落在屋顶上。
senses.why: What rarely happens stands out from the background, and the word easily takes on the sense of rare.
senses.whyCN: 很少发生的事会从背景里凸显出来，于是这个词自然带出「稀奇」的意思。

senses.title: Different from others in a good way
senses.definition: used with approval of something special or original
senses.definitionCN: 用于赞许某个特别或有创意的做法
senses.example: They chose an unusual route through the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们挑了一条穿过老城的别致路线。
senses.why: What separates itself from habit can separate itself well, so the word takes on approval of the original.
senses.whyCN: 与习惯拉开距离的东西也可能拉得漂亮，于是这个词带上了对「有创意」的赞许。

senses.title: Odd in a way that worries people
senses.definition: used of conditions or behaviour that suggest something is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 形容暗示出问题的状况或行为
senses.example: The doctor noticed an unusual rhythm in the pulse.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到脉搏有一种异常节律。
senses.why: Once something departs from the usual, a departure can also warn that something has gone wrong.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物偏离常规，这种偏离也能成为「哪里出了毛病」的警报。

senses.title: Exceptional in degree
senses.definition: used with a following adjective to mean exceptionally
senses.definitionCN: 后接形容词，表示程度格外地
senses.example: The room fell unusually quiet when she entered.
senses.exampleCN: 她进门时，房间异常安静下来。
senses.why: A departure from the customary, applied to a degree, becomes the adverb sense of going beyond the normal level.
senses.whyCN: 偏离常规一旦用在程度上，就成了「超出平常水准」的副词义。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective formed from the noun use in its old sense of habit.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在一个由 use 旧义「习惯」构成的形容词上。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and marks the opposite of a quality.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，表示某一性质的反面。

items.en: Usus meant use or practice, with the verb uti, to use.
items.cn: usus 意为「使用、实践」，动词为 uti（使用）。

items.en: The noun passed into French as us, and the adjective usuel meant customary.
items.cn: 这个名词在法语中作 us，形容词 usuel 意为「惯常的」。

items.en: Usual settles in English meaning customary, derived from use as a habit.
items.cn: usual 在英语中定型为「惯常的」，其根源是「习惯」义的使用。

items.en: Unusual grows from that and widens to rare sights, odd behaviour, and unusual weather.
items.cn: unusual 由此生长出来，并扩展到罕见景象、反常行为与反常天气。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the use family and its adverbs, while the near-meaning group collects words for the rare and the odd.
note.cn: 形近组沿 use 词族及其副词展开，近义组汇集表示罕见与奇特的说法。

examples.en: The garden was full of unusual plants from the south.

examples.en: He gave the question an unusually long look before answering.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one white bird standing among grey ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰鸽群里站着一只白鸽。

branches.en: The habit branch: this is not how it normally goes.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：平时不是这个样子。

branches.en: The rarity branch: people stop and stare.
branches.cn: 罕见分支：人们停下来张望。

branches.en: The praise branch: different in a welcome way.
branches.cn: 赞许分支：不同得让人欣然接受。

branches.en: The warning branch: a sign that something is off.
branches.cn: 警示分支：某个地方不对的信号。

branches.en: The degree branch: exceptionally, before an adjective.
branches.cn: 程度分支：放在形容词前表示格外。

intro.en: A native negative prefix over an adjective whose base noun still lives in common use.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在一个底名词仍在常用词汇中的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is uti and its noun usus, from which usualis was formed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根为 uti 及其名词 usus，usualis 由后者构成。

items.example: Custom is a kind of use.
items.exampleCN: 习俗即是一种习惯性的使用。

items.example: Usus gives usuel and then usual.
items.exampleCN: usus 派生出 usuel，再成为 usual。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: He came at the usual time.

items.meaning: the way words or things are used
items.exampleCN: 英语的用法在这里不同。

latinEntries.meaning: to use, to make use of

senses.title: Of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心智的：发生在头脑里的事
senses.definition: relating to the mind or to thinking, as opposed to the body
senses.definitionCN: 与心智或思维有关的，与身体相对
senses.example: Reading a map is a mental skill, not a physical one.
senses.exampleCN: 看地图是一项心智技能，而不是体力技能。
senses.why: Mental entered English in the early 15th century from Late Latin mentalis, from Latin mens 'mind'. The adjective simply marks what happens inside the head.
senses.whyCN: mental 于 15 世纪初从晚期拉丁语 mentalis 进入英语，源自拉丁语 mens“心智”。这个形容词只标记在头脑内部发生的事。

senses.title: Psychological health
senses.titleCN: 心理的：情绪与心理状态
senses.definition: relating to a person's emotional and psychological condition
senses.definitionCN: 与一个人的情绪与心理状况有关的
senses.example: The clinic offers mental health services for teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为青少年提供心理健康服务。
senses.why: Mental health is recorded from 1803. Once the mind has a health of its own, the adjective moves from describing thought to naming a field of care.
senses.whyCN: mental health 自 1803 年有记录。一旦心智有了自己的健康，这个形容词就从描述思维转为命名一个照护领域。

senses.title: Of the soul
senses.titleCN: 精神的：心灵层面的旧义
senses.definition: in older use, relating to the soul or the inner, spiritual life
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，与灵魂或内在精神生活有关的
senses.example: The old prayer asks for mental peace rather than bodily comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的祷文求的是心灵的安宁，而不是身体的舒适。
senses.why: In Middle English, mental also meant 'of the soul, spiritual'. Before medicine divided mind from body, the word covered the whole inner life.
senses.whyCN: 在中古英语里，mental 也意为“灵魂的、精神的”。在医学把心智与身体分开之前，这个词覆盖的是整个内在生活。

senses.title: Intellectual effort
senses.titleCN: 脑力的：劳动落在头脑上
senses.definition: requiring or involving thought and intellect rather than physical work
senses.definitionCN: 需要或涉及思考与智力，而非体力劳动
senses.example: Mental labour can exhaust a person as surely as lifting does.
senses.exampleCN: 脑力劳动照样能把人累垮，就像搬运一样。
senses.why: From the 1520s the word meant 'done or performed in the mind'. Effort shifts from the muscles to the brain, and the adjective follows it.
senses.whyCN: 自 16 世纪 20 年代起，这个词意为“在头脑中完成的”。力气从肌肉转到大脑，形容词也跟着转了过去。

senses.title: Done inside the head
senses.titleCN: 默算默想：不外化的过程
senses.definition: performed silently in the mind, without writing or speaking
senses.definitionCN: 不写出来也不说出来，在脑中默默完成
senses.example: She did the sum mentally and wrote only the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她心算了那道题，只写下答案。
senses.why: Mental arithmetic keeps the whole operation invisible. The adjective marks work that leaves no trace until the result appears.
senses.whyCN: 心算把整个运算过程藏了起来。这个形容词标记的是那种直到结果出现才留下痕迹的劳动。

senses.title: Psychiatric illness
senses.definition: relating to psychiatric illness, its institutions and its patients
senses.definitionCN: 与精神疾病、其机构及病人有关的
senses.example: He was admitted to a mental hospital after the second episode.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次发作后，他被送进了精神病院。
senses.why: Mental patient is recorded from 1859 and mental hospital from 1891. Once institutions exist, the adjective becomes a clinical address.
senses.whyCN: mental patient 自 1859 年有记录，mental hospital 自 1891 年有记录。一旦机构存在，这个形容词就变成了一个临床门牌号。

senses.title: Slang: crazy
senses.titleCN: 口语：发疯的、脑子有毛病的
senses.definition: in informal British English, crazy or wildly unreasonable
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中，指发疯的或极不合理的
senses.example: You are mental if you think that jump is safe.
senses.exampleCN: 你要是觉得那样跳下去没事，那你真是疯了。
senses.why: The slang sense 'crazy, deranged' is recorded from 1927, probably from combinations such as mental patient. A clinical label leaks into the playground.
senses.whyCN: “发疯的、精神错乱的”这一俚语义自 1927 年有记录，很可能来自 mental patient 一类的组合。临床标签漏进了操场。

senses.title: Slang noun: a mad person
senses.definition: in informal British English, a person who is mentally ill or behaves wildly
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中，指精神失常或行为失控的人
senses.example: The driver was a complete mental and should never have been on the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那个司机完全是个疯子，根本就不该上路。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun for a person who has the quality. Here the medical label becomes an insult.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接变成指人的名词。在这里，医学标签变成了骂人的话。

senses.title: Legal and clinical capacity
senses.definition: in law and medicine, used of a person's ability to understand, decide and be responsible
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与医学中，指一个人理解、决定与承担责任的能力
senses.example: The court asked whether the accused had the mental capacity to understand the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 法院问的是被告是否有心智能力理解这项指控。
senses.why: Law needs the mind as a measurable fact, not a metaphor. Mental capacity turns the inner life into something a form can record.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要把心智当成可测量的事实，而不是比喻。mental capacity 把内在生活变成表格上可以填写的东西。

intro.en: Mental comes from Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind' through Late Latin mentalis. Its root is PIE *men- 'to think'. The medical and middle senses of the letters 'ment' belong to other roots entirely. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mental 经由晚期拉丁语 mentalis 来自拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”。它的词根是原始印欧语 *men-“思考”。字母 ment 所对应的“医疗”与“中间”两族词，属于完全另外的词根。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded as 'in, of, or pertaining to the mind; characteristic of the intellect'. It came from Late Latin mentalis 'of the mind', an adjective built on Latin mens.
items.cn: 最早记录为“在心智之中的、属于心智的；智力特征的”。它来自晚期拉丁语 mentalis“心智的”，是建立在拉丁语 mens 之上的形容词。

items.en: Latin mens (genitive mentis) means 'mind, intellect, thought, intention'. The stem ment- is what English borrows in mental, mentality and dementia.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）意为“心智、智力、思想、意图”。英语在 mental、mentality、dementia 中借入的正是词干 ment-。

items.en: The root *men- (1) means 'to think'. It also lies behind English mind, a native Germanic cousin of Latin mens rather than a borrowing from it.
items.cn: 词根 *men-（第一支）意为“思考”。它也是英语 mind 的来源——mind 是拉丁语 mens 在日耳曼语里的本族表亲，而不是从拉丁语借来的。

items.en: Mental also meant 'of the soul, spiritual' in Middle English. The word covered the inner life before medicine separated mind from body.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，mental 也意为“灵魂的、精神的”。在医学把心智与身体分开之前，这个词覆盖的是整个内在生活。

items.en: The sense 'done or performed in the mind' is recorded, the sense behind mental arithmetic and mental rehearsal.
items.cn: 记录到“在头脑中完成的”这一义项，它正是 mental arithmetic 与 mental rehearsal 背后的意思。

items.en: Mental health is recorded from 1803, mental illness from 1819, mental patient from 1859 and mental hospital from 1891. The slang sense 'crazy, deranged' follows in 1927, probably from those combinations.
items.cn: mental health 自 1803 年有记录，mental illness 自 1819 年，mental patient 自 1859 年，mental hospital 自 1891 年。俚语义“发疯的、精神错乱的”在 1927 年出现，很可能来自这些组合。

note.en: The first group separates the native noun mind, the derived noun mentality, the adverb and the person word. The second group places mental against the adjectives it is most often confused with, including its usual opposite.
note.cn: 第一组区分本族名词 mind、派生名词 mentality、副词与指人的词。第二组把 mental 与最常混淆的几个形容词放在一起，包括它通常的对立面。

entries.definition: the faculty of thinking, or a person's thoughts and attention. It is the native English cousin of Latin mens, while mental is the borrowed adjective built on mens.
entries.definitionCN: 思维的能力，或一个人的想法与注意力。它是拉丁语 mens 在英语里的本族表亲，而 mental 是建立在 mens 上的借入形容词。

entries.definition: a typical way of thinking, or the level of a person's intellectual power. It is a countable pattern of mind, not a synonym of mental.
entries.definitionCN: 典型的思维方式，或一个人的智力水平。它是可数的思维模式，不是 mental 的同义词。

entries.definition: in the mind, or with respect to the mind. It modifies a verb ('mentally rehearsed') where mental would modify a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中，或就心智而言。它修饰动词（如 mentally rehearsed），而 mental 修饰名词。

entries.definition: a performer who appears to read minds, or a believer in mentalism. It never means 'a mental person'.
entries.definitionCN: 看似能读心的表演者，或心灵主义的信奉者。它从不表示“精神失常的人”。

entries.definition: relating to the study of the mind and behaviour, or to a person's inner emotional state. It is more technical than mental and often replaces it in careful writing.
entries.definitionCN: 与心理学研究或一个人的内在情绪状态有关的。它比 mental 更技术化，在严谨写作中常替代 mental。

entries.definition: relating to the medical treatment of mental illness. It names the clinic, while mental can still be a neutral word for the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病的医学治疗有关的。它命名的是临床，而 mental 仍可中性地指心智。

entries.definition: relating to the intellect and its exercise, especially in learning and analysis. It praises the work of the mind; mental merely locates it.
entries.definitionCN: 与智力及其运用有关的，尤其在学习与分析中。它赞赏头脑的工作；mental 只标明位置。

entries.definition: relating to the body rather than the mind. The pair mental and physical organises everyday talk about health, training and fatigue.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体而非心智有关的。mental 与 physical 这一对词组织起了日常关于健康、训练与疲劳的说法。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind', PIE *men- 'to think', the English cousin mind, and the family mentality, mentally, dementia.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”、原始印欧语 *men-“思考”、英语表亲 mind，以及 mentality、mentally、dementia 词族。

normal.en: mens, mentis means 'mind'. Mental is the adjective of that noun: whatever belongs to the mind.
normal.cn: mens、mentis 意为“心智”。mental 就是这个名词的形容词：一切属于心智的东西。

normal.en: The root *men- means 'to think', and it also gives the native English word mind. Mental is the borrowed twin of mind.
normal.cn: 词根 *men- 意为“思考”，它也给出英语本族词 mind。mental 是 mind 的借入版双胞胎。

normal.en: mentality is mental plus -ity: not the mind itself but its habitual shape, a way of thinking.
normal.cn: mentality 是 mental 加 -ity：不是心智本身，而是它习惯性的形状，即一种思维方式。

normal.en: mentally is the adverb: it tells you where the work happens, as in mentally rehearsed.
normal.cn: mentally 是副词：它告诉你工作发生在哪里，如 mentally rehearsed（在脑中排练）。

normal.en: Keep the fixed phrases straight: mental health, mental illness, mental hospital. These are clinical and neutral, not insults.
normal.cn: 把固定搭配记准：mental health、mental illness、mental hospital。这些是临床且中性的说法，不是骂人。

abstract.en: Picture a lit lamp inside a skull. Nobody outside can see the flame, only its light falling on what the person does next.
abstract.cn: 想象颅骨里点着一盏灯。外面的人看不见火焰，只看见火光落在这个人接下来的动作上。

abstract.en: The same lamp can be described in three registers: mental is everyday, psychological is scientific, psychiatric is clinical. One flame, three vocabularies.
abstract.cn: 同一盏灯可以用三种语域描述：mental 是日常的，psychological 是科学的，psychiatric 是临床的。一团火焰，三套词汇。

abstract.en: Because the light is invisible, the word is easily abused: it can name care, or it can become an insult. The phrase tells you which.
abstract.cn: 正因为光看不见，这个词容易被滥用：它可以命名照护，也可以变成侮辱。是哪个，要看它所在的短语。

examples.en: The injury healed in weeks, but the mental scars took years.
examples.cn: 伤在几周内就愈合了，但心理上的伤痕花了好几年。

examples.en: He ran the whole interview in his head, mentally correcting every answer.
examples.cn: 他在脑子里把整场面试过了一遍，逐条修正每个回答。

examples.en: The report calls for better mental health care in rural schools.
examples.cn: 报告呼吁改善乡村学校的心理健康照护。

dict_mnemonic.text: “门头儿”——门头儿里面亮着一盏灯，那是脑子里转个不停的念头 → mental 心理的、心智的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”，词根 *men- 意为“思考”，核心是“在头脑内部进行的活动”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mental, all lit by one lamp inside the skull: first it simply marks where thought happens, then it names health, effort, silence, illness, insult and finally a legal fact.
sensesIntro.cn: mental 的九个义项都被颅骨里的同一盏灯照亮：它先只标记思考发生的位置，继而命名健康、劳动、沉默、疾病、辱骂，最后成为一种法律事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning inside a skull, visible only through what the person does.
core.cn: 核心意象：颅骨里燃着的一盏灯，只能通过这个人的举动被看见。

branches.en: THE INNER LIFE: the oldest sense marks the mind, and once also the soul, as a region distinct from the body.
branches.cn: 内在生活：最老的义项标记心智——也曾标记灵魂——作为区别于身体的一个区域。

branches.en: HEALTH: mental health gives the inner life a condition that can be cared for.
branches.cn: 健康：mental health 给内在生活一个可以被照护的状态。

branches.en: EFFORT: thought becomes labour, and labour can be done with no visible trace.
branches.cn: 劳动：思考变成劳作，而这种劳作可以不留可见痕迹。

branches.en: ILLNESS: the clinical label builds hospitals and patients, and then turns into a playground insult.
branches.cn: 疾病：临床标签建起了医院与病人，随后又变成操场上的骂人话。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: slang decides who is crazy; law decides who can understand and be responsible.
branches.cn: 判断：俚语义断定谁疯了；法律则断定谁能理解、谁能负责。

intro.en: Mental is Latin ment- 'mind' plus the adjective ending -al. The suffix is productive in English; the stem ment- is not a free word, but it recurs in mentality, dementia and mentalize.
intro.cn: mental 是拉丁语 ment-“心智”加形容词词尾 -al。这个后缀在英语里能产；词干 ment- 不能单独成词，却在 mentality、dementia、mentalize 中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin mentalis was built on Latin mens (genitive mentis) 'mind', from PIE *men- 'to think'. The same root supplies dementia (de- 'away' + mens) and the native English mind.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 mentalis 建立在拉丁语 mens（属格 mentis）“心智”之上，源自原始印欧语 *men-“思考”。同一词根也给出 dementia（de-“离开”+ mens）以及英语本族词 mind。

items.meaning: of or relating to the mind
items.meaningCN: 心理的；心智的（ment- 心智 + -al 形容词词尾）
items.example: The test measures mental rather than manual speed.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测的是思维速度，而不是手的速度。

items.meaning: a way of thinking; mental character
items.meaningCN: 心态；思维方式（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The team's mentality changed after the first win.
items.exampleCN: 首胜之后，球队的心态变了。

items.meaning: in the mind; with respect to the mind
items.meaningCN: 心理上；在脑中（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She counted the steps mentally before jumping.
items.exampleCN: 起跳前她在心里数了步子。

items.meaning: a mind-reading performer; a believer in mentalism
items.meaningCN: 读心术表演者；心灵主义者（-ist 指人）
items.example: The mentalist guessed the card without touching it.
items.exampleCN: 那位读心术表演者没碰牌就猜中了。

items.meaning: the view that mind or consciousness is fundamental
items.meaningCN: 心灵主义；唯心论（-ism 表学说）
items.example: Mentalism treats consciousness as the basic stuff of reality.
items.exampleCN: 心灵主义把意识当作现实的基本材料。

items.meaning: relating to mentalism or to explanations in mental terms
items.meaningCN: 心灵主义的；用心理术语解释的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 行为主义者拒斥用心理术语所作的解释。

items.meaning: to understand behaviour as arising from mental states
items.meaningCN: 心智化；把行为理解为心理状态的产物（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: Children learn to mentalize through play.
items.exampleCN: 儿童在游戏中学着理解他人的心理。

items.meaning: a condition in which the mind has gone away
items.meaningCN: 痴呆；认知功能衰退（de- 离开 + ment- 心智 + -ia 状态）
items.example: The early signs of dementia were mistaken for tiredness.
items.exampleCN: 痴呆的早期迹象被误认为是疲劳。

items.meaning: out of one's mind; wildly foolish
items.meaningCN: 精神错乱的；荒唐的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The plan was demented from the first page.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划从第一页起就荒唐透顶。

items.meaning: an object kept as a reminder
items.meaningCN: 纪念物；使人想起某事的物件（源自拉丁语祈使式“记得”）
items.example: He kept the ticket as a memento of the trip.
items.exampleCN: 他把那张票留着，作为那次旅行的纪念。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 失去理智的；精神错乱的

definition_en: a formal meeting, a period of an activity, a period of study, or a period of use of a computer system
core_image: 长桌旁，人们依次坐下，会议记录翻到新的一页
scene: 委员会在周一召开了一次会议。 The committee held a session on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 session 是「会议」（第 1 个义项）；句意：委员会在周一召开了一次会议。

senses.title: Formal meeting
senses.definition: a formal meeting of a group or official body
senses.definitionCN: 团体或官方机构的正式会议
senses.example: The committee held a session on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在周一召开了一次会议。

senses.title: Period of activity
senses.definition: a period of time used for one activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项活动的一段时间
senses.example: The band played a long session.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队演奏了很长时间。
senses.why: An activity can fill a sitting.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动可以占满一次「坐定」的时间。

senses.title: Period of study

senses.why: Teaching is organized in sittings.

intro.en: Session comes from Latin sessio, a sitting, from sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: session 源自拉丁语 sessio（坐、会期），来自动词 sedere（坐）。

items.en: Sedere meant to sit.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐。

items.en: Sessio meant a sitting or a meeting.
items.cn: sessio 意为坐、会期。

items.en: Session kept the sense of a sitting.
items.cn: session 保留了「坐定开会」的含义。

items.en: Session named a formal meeting.
items.cn: session 指正式会议。

items.en: Session extended to study and computers.
items.cn: session 扩展到学期时段与计算机会话。

note.en: Session is compared with similar-looking words and with words for meetings.
note.cn: 把 session 与形近词以及表示会议的字词作比较。

abstract.cn: 坐在一起，就是给一段时间一个共同的形状。

abstract.en: Every meeting is a small stage with a beginning and an end.
abstract.cn: 每一场会议都是有小幕起落的小舞台。

abstract.en: A session ends, but what was decided may keep standing.
abstract.cn: 会期会结束，但作出的决定可能一直立着。

definition_en: to give all your attention to one thing, or to make something stronger by removing water
core_image: 一束散开的光被透镜收成一个亮点
scene: 图书馆里，她把手机翻面扣在桌上才开始读书。 He turned off the music so he could concentrate on the chapter.
sceneCN: 这里 concentrate 指「集中注意力」（第 1 个义项：把心思放在一件事上）；句意是他关掉音乐，好把注意力集中在这一章上。

senses.title: Focus your attention
senses.definition: to give all your attention to one thing
senses.definitionCN: 把全部注意力放在一件事上
senses.example: She concentrated on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 她专心看地图。
senses.why: The mind scatters easily, so it must be gathered onto one point.
senses.whyCN: 心思容易散开，所以必须收拢到一个点上。

senses.title: Bring together in one place
senses.definition: to bring things or people together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把事物或人聚到一个地方
senses.example: The troops were concentrated near the border.
senses.exampleCN: 部队集中在边境附近。
senses.why: The same gathering motion works for armies and for attention.
senses.whyCN: 这种收拢的动作既能用于军队，也能用于注意力。

senses.title: Make stronger by removing water
senses.definition: to make a liquid stronger by taking water out of it
senses.definitionCN: 去掉水分使液体更浓
senses.example: The juice is concentrated before shipping.
senses.exampleCN: 果汁在运输前先被浓缩。
senses.why: Less water means the same substance sits in a smaller space.
senses.whyCN: 水分少了，同样的物质就集中在更小的空间里。

intro.en: Concentrate is built from Latin com-, together, and centrum, the centre: to bring to one centre.
intro.cn: concentrate 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 centrum（中心）构成，意为聚到一个中心。

items.en: Centrum meant the middle point of a circle.
items.cn: centrum 指圆的中心点。

items.en: Concentrare meant to bring several things to one centre.
items.cn: concentrare 意为把几样东西聚到一个中心。

items.en: French concentrer applied the word to liquids and to thought.
items.cn: 法语 concentrer 把它同时用于液体与思想。

items.en: English concentrate first meant to bring to a common centre.
items.cn: 英语 concentrate 最初指聚到共同的中心。

items.en: It now covers attention, troops and strong liquids.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖注意力、部队与浓液体。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to concentrate, and the meaning group names other words for gathering or focusing.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 concentrate 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示聚集与聚焦的词。

the ability to focus attention
strong because water has been removed

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with light through a lens, then move to troops in one place and to strong juice.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从穿过透镜的光开始，再走到聚集一处的部队与浓果汁。

normal.en: Con- is together and centre is the middle, so concentrate is to bring everything to the middle.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，centre 是中心，concentrate 就是把一切收拢到中心。

normal.en: A lens concentrates light into one bright point.

normal.en: Concentrate on one page and the other pages go quiet.

normal.en: Concentrated juice has less water and more taste.

normal.en: The noun concentration covers both attention and strength of a mixture.

abstract.cn: 想象放大镜在纸上烧出一个小点。

abstract.en: Picture many roads all ending at one square.
abstract.cn: 想象许多条路都通向同一个广场。

abstract.en: Picture a wide river squeezed into a narrow channel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条宽河被收进窄窄的河道。

examples.en: It is hard to concentrate in a noisy room.
examples.cn: 在吵闹的房间里很难集中注意力。

examples.en: The general concentrated his forces near the river.
examples.cn: 将军把兵力集中在河边。

examples.en: The factory concentrates the milk before packing it.
examples.cn: 工厂先把牛奶浓缩再包装。

root: 源自拉丁语 com（一起）与 centrum（中心），本义是聚到一个中心，后引申为集中注意力、聚集力量与浓缩液体。

branches.en: Both senses make one place or one liquid hold more.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让一个地方或一种液体装得更多。

definition_zh: 捻；搓；拧；扭弯；缠绕；（故事的）转折；曲折；拧转的动作
definition_en: to wind two or more strands together, to bend or turn something out of shape, or an unexpected change in a story or situation
core_image: 两股绳被反方向拧在一起，拧着拧着就拐了个弯
scene: 奶奶坐在门槛上搓麻绳，两股线在她掌心越缠越紧。 She learned to twist flax into strong rope as a girl.
sceneCN: 这里 twist 是动词「捻、搓」（第 1 个义项：把丝线拧合成绳）；句意为她少女时代就学会把亚麻捻成结实的绳子。

pos.zh: 名词：拧转；（故事）转折；曲折；扭伤；麻花状物

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「弯弯曲曲的；曲折的」
由本词过去分词转作形容词，义为「扭曲的；（心智）反常的」
由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「缠绕者；难题；（口语）龙卷风（tornado 的别称）」

senses.title: To wind strands together
senses.definition: to wind two or more threads, fibres or wires around each other to form a cord or rope
senses.definitionCN: 把两股或多股线、纤维或金属丝相互缠绕成绳线
senses.example: The villagers twist palm leaves into twine for fishing nets.
senses.exampleCN: 村民把棕榈叶捻成搓渔网用的细绳。
senses.why: The core image is two strands rolled in opposite directions so they grip each other.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是两股线朝相反方向滚动，从而互相咬合。

senses.title: To turn a controlling knob or cap
senses.definition: to turn something such as a cap, lid or key with a rotating movement
senses.definitionCN: 以旋转动作拧动瓶盖、盖子或钥匙等
senses.example: She twisted off the jam jar lid and handed it over.
senses.exampleCN: 她拧下果酱瓶盖递了过去。
senses.why: A cap held by opposing grips comes loose only by rolling the hands apart.
senses.whyCN: 瓶盖要靠两手反向滚动才能松动。

senses.title: To bend or wrench out of shape
senses.definition: to bend, wrench or force something out of its natural shape
senses.definitionCN: 把某物弯曲、扳扭或强行弄离原有形状
senses.example: The crash twisted the bicycle's front wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车把自行车前轮撞得变了形。
senses.why: Force applied unevenly rotates part of an object away from the rest; the shape spirals.
senses.whyCN: 不均匀的力使物体一部分相对其余部分转开，形状呈螺旋状偏离。

senses.title: To injure a joint by wrenching
senses.definition: to hurt a joint such as an ankle or wrist by suddenly wrenching it
senses.definitionCN: 因突然的扭转而扭伤脚踝、手腕等关节
senses.example: He twisted his knee stepping off the last stair.
senses.exampleCN: 下最后一级台阶时他扭伤了膝盖。
senses.why: The joint is the body's most turnable part; a wrong turn strains it.
senses.whyCN: 关节是身体最易转动的部位；转错方向便拉伤。

senses.title: To wind or coil around
senses.definition: to wrap one thing around another, often in a spiral
senses.definitionCN: 把一物缠绕在另一物上，常呈螺旋状
senses.example: Vines twist around the old fence posts every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 每年夏天藤蔓都缠绕在旧篱笆桩上。
senses.why: The rope-making motion, applied by nature, wraps one thing about another.
senses.whyCN: 制绳的旋转动作由自然施加，便成了缠绕。

senses.title: To move in a winding way
senses.definition: to follow a winding, bending course, as a road, river or body may do
senses.definitionCN: 沿蜿蜒弯曲的路线行进，如道路、河流或身体
senses.example: The mountain road twists down toward the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山路蜿蜒而下，通向谷底。
senses.why: A bent line is one that keeps turning; winding is repeated small twists.
senses.whyCN: 弯线就是不断转向的线；蜿蜒是许多次小幅的拧转。

senses.title: An unexpected change in a story
senses.definition: an unexpected development or change of direction in a story, situation or plan
senses.definitionCN: 故事、局势或计划中出人意料的变化或转向
senses.example: The trial took a twist when a new witness appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 一位新证人出现后，庭审出现了转折。
senses.why: The bent shape is projected onto events: when the straight line of the plot suddenly bends, that bend is the twist.
senses.whyCN: 把弯折之形投射到事件上：情节的直线突然拐弯，这个弯就是 twist。

senses.title: A spiralling shape or object
senses.definition: a shape made by winding something around itself, such as a curl of peel or a piece of twisted bread
senses.definitionCN: 由缠绕自身而成的形状，如柑皮卷或麻花状面点
senses.example: The barman garnished the glass with a twist of lemon peel.
senses.exampleCN: 调酒师用一小卷柠檬皮装饰酒杯。
senses.why: The noun freezes the rope picture into a small object you can see and hold.
senses.whyCN: 名词把制绳画面冻结成一件看得见、拿得住的小物件。

senses.title: To distort the meaning of words
senses.definition: to change or present someone's words so that they mean something unfair or unintended
senses.definitionCN: 改动或呈现某人的话，使其带有不公或非本意的含义
senses.example: The tabloid twisted her remarks into an accusation.
senses.exampleCN: 小报把她的评论曲解成一项指控。
senses.why: Words are like strands: pulled askew, they no longer lie straight and true.
senses.whyCN: 话语如绳股：被斜着拽动，便不再笔直属实。

senses.title: A twisted mind: mental distortion
senses.titleCN: 反常的心智；扭曲的观念
senses.definition: in describing a person or thinking as twisted, mentally distorted or unhealthily turned
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或思想 twisted，指心智扭曲、想法反常
senses.example: The villain's twisted logic blames everyone but himself.
senses.exampleCN: 反派的扭曲逻辑把过错归咎于除自己以外的所有人。
senses.why: The wrenched shape becomes a metaphor for wrenched judgment; what should run straight has been bent.
senses.whyCN: 被拧弯的形状成为被扭曲的判断的比喻；本应笔直的思路被掰弯了。

intro.en: Twist descends from an Old English word for a rope made of twisted strands.
intro.cn: twist 源自古英语中指「用股线拧成的绳索」的词。

items.en: *dwo- 'two' is generally reconstructed at the base of the family, since twisting joins two strands.
items.cn: 一般认为词族底层是重构形式 *dwo-「二」，因为拧转正是把两股合在一起。

items.en: Old English twist meant 'a cord, a twisted rope', recorded for rope-making and sail-making.
items.cn: 古英语 twist 意为「细绳、拧成的绳索」，见于制绳与制帆的记载。

items.en: The word kept the rope sense and began to name the winding motion itself.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了绳索义，并开始指拧转这一动作本身。

items.en: The verb widened to wrenching, coiling and winding courses; the relationship to the numeral two is generally accepted but the exact morphological path is uncertain.
items.cn: 十五、十六世纪动词扩展到扳扭、缠绕与蜿蜒；与数词「二」的关系一般被接受，但确切形态演变路径不确定。

items.en: The figurative senses flourished in fiction: the plot twist became a stock term of storytelling.
items.cn: 十九世纪比喻义在小说中大放异彩：plot twist 成为叙事的固定术语。

items.en: Today the word covers rope, joints, roads, plots and personalities alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词同时涵盖绳索、关节、道路、情节与性格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the tw- family and sound-alike words; the near-meaning group gathers winding, bending and turning words.
note.cn: 形近组收 tw- 词族与音近词；近义组收缠绕、弯曲与转动类词。

entries.definition: Strong string made of twisted strands, or to wind around; the direct rope relative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「细绳；缠绕」，是直接的绳索同族词。

entries.definition: Two times; shares the old two-strand numeral root in origin but counts instead of winding.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「两次」，词源上同样关联「二股」这一古老数词根，但表示计数而非缠绕。

entries.definition: The joint between hand and arm; long associated with turning and twisting, though the exact common origin with twist is debated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手腕」，历来与「拧转」相关，但与 twist 是否同源尚有争议。

entries.definition: A cloth woven with a diagonal pattern of crossing threads; another textile word of the tw- weaving family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斜纹布」，指线股斜向交织的织物，同属 tw- 织造词族。

entries.definition: To spin quickly and lightly; looks like twist but is a separate, probably blended word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「轻快旋转」，形似 twist，但可能是另一混合来源的词。

entries.definition: To coil something around in loops; emphasizes the wrapping rather than the gripping of strands.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缠绕；盘绕」，强调环绕成圈，而非两股咬合。

entries.definition: To gather into rings or a spiral; the result is loops, not joined strands.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「盘绕成圈」，结果呈环状，而非股线拧合。

entries.definition: To twist suddenly and violently, often injuring something; stress falls on the force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「猛拧；猛扭」，常致损伤，强调暴烈的用力。

entries.definition: A curve winding around a centre, or to move in such a curve; geometric in flavor.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「螺旋；盘旋」，偏几何意味。

entries.definition: To turn aside suddenly from a straight course; the turning without the winding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「突然偏离直线方向」，只有转向而无缠绕。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real rope root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的绳索词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Old English twist was itself a cord: the word began life as rope.
normal.cn: 古英语 twist 本义就是细绳：这个词生来就是绳子。

normal.en: Twine, twill, twist: the tw- family is all about joining two strands.
normal.cn: twine、twill、twist：tw- 词族全都围绕「两股相合」。

normal.en: Twist one's ankle is the body's rope kinked the wrong way.
normal.cn: twist one's ankle 就是身体的绳索拐错了方向。

normal.en: A twist in the plot is the story's rope taking a sudden bend.
normal.cn: 情节的 twist 是故事的绳子突然拐了个弯。

normal.en: Twist off a lid: roll your hands apart and the cap gives way.
normal.cn: twist off a lid：两手反向一滚，盖子就松了。

abstract.en: Picture two threads rolling toward each other between your palms, gripping tighter with every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象两根线在你掌心相向滚动，每转一圈咬得更紧。

abstract.en: A road that twists is one that cannot say a straight sentence.
abstract.cn: 蜿蜒的路就是一句说不出直线的话。

abstract.en: Twisted words are strands pulled out of line: still there, but no longer true.
abstract.cn: 被歪曲的话语是拽离了直线绳股：还在那里，却不再属实。

examples.en: She twisted three coloured threads into a friendship bracelet.
examples.cn: 她把三根彩色丝线捻成一条友谊手链。

examples.en: The film ends with a twist nobody in the cinema saw coming.
examples.cn: 影片的结局来了一个全场无人料到的转折。

examples.en: Reporters accused the spokesman of twisting the minister's words.
examples.cn: 记者指责发言人歪曲部长的原话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特为斯特」——特意把两股线拧成一股绳：捻、拧、缠

root: 古英语 twist「细绳、拧成的绳索」，一般认为可追溯至原始印欧语 *dwo-「二」（重构形式），因拧转即合二股；与 twine、twill、twin、twice 同属 tw- 词族；与数词二的确切形态关联存在不确定性。

sensesIntro.en: The ten senses of twist all grow from one coiled picture: making rope, turning caps, wrenching shapes, twisting joints and roads, bending plots, curling peel, distorting words and minds.
sensesIntro.cn: twist 的十个义项都从同一幅缠绕画面生长：搓绳、拧盖、扳弯形状、扭伤关节、蜿蜒道路、情节拐弯、柑皮成卷、话语与心智被扭曲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two strands roll in opposite directions and grip into one rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股线反向滚动，咬合成一根绳。

branches.en: THE ROPE: making, wrapping and freezing the coil into objects like peel twists.
branches.cn: 绳索线：制绳、缠裹，并把盘绕冻结成柑皮卷之类的物件。

branches.en: THE FORCE: turning caps, wrenching shapes and straining joints.
branches.cn: 用力线：拧盖、扳弯形状与拉伤关节。

branches.en: THE PATH: repeated small turns make a winding road.
branches.cn: 路径线：多次小幅转向织成蜿蜒的路。

branches.en: THE STORY: the straight line of events takes a sudden bend.
branches.cn: 故事线：事件的直线突然拐弯。

branches.en: THE MIND: words and judgments pulled out of true.
branches.cn: 心智线：话语与判断被拽离本相。

intro.en: Twist is a single native root, but its tw- family spreads across rope, cloth, kinship and counting.
intro.cn: twist 是单个本族词根，但其 tw- 词族横跨绳索、织物、亲属与计数。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the Indo-European base is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；印欧词基属重构形式。

items.example: The noun is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是可考的最早形式。

items.example: It forms twisted cloth and twisted minds.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 twisted（拧过的）布料与扭曲的心智。
它构成 twisty（弯弯曲曲的）道路。

items.example: The sister word keeps the rope sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个同族词保留了绳索义。

items.example: It shows the family in weaving.
items.exampleCN: 它显示该词族在织造中的身影。

items.meaning: the turning joint of the arm
items.example: Its link with twist is old but debated.
items.exampleCN: 它与 twist 的关联古老但有争议。

items.example: It names the violent member of the turning family.
items.exampleCN: 它命名了转动家族中暴烈的一员。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「弯弯曲曲的；曲折的」
由本词过去分词转作形容词，义为「扭曲的；（心智）反常的」
由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「缠绕者；难题；（口语）龙卷风」

definition_en: a large meeting where people discuss a subject or share ideas
core_image: 长桌两旁坐满人，每人面前一支麦克风
scene: 各地医生聚在大厅里交流新研究。 She met her future partner at a medical conference.
sceneCN: 这里 conference 指「会议」（第 1 个义项：多人聚集讨论专业问题的场合）；句意是她在一次医学会议上遇见了未来的伴侣。

senses.title: A large formal meeting
senses.definition: a large meeting where people discuss a shared subject
senses.definitionCN: 许多人聚集讨论共同主题的大型会议
senses.example: The annual conference drew two thousand guests.
senses.exampleCN: 年度会议吸引了两千名来宾。
senses.why: A shared subject gives strangers a reason to sit in one room.
senses.whyCN: 共同的主题让陌生人有了坐进同一个房间的理由。

senses.title: A private discussion
senses.definition: a private discussion between a few people before a decision
senses.definitionCN: 少数人在做决定前的私下商谈
senses.example: After a short conference, the two sides agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 短暂商谈之后，双方达成了一致。
senses.why: Some words are said best when only a few people are listening.
senses.whyCN: 有些话在只有少数人听的时候最好说。

intro.en: Conference comes from Latin conferentia, a bringing together, from conferre, to bring together.
intro.cn: conference 来自拉丁语 conferentia，意为聚集，源自 conferre（带到一起）。

items.en: Conferre meant to carry people or ideas into one place.
items.cn: conferre 意为把人或想法带到同一个地方。

items.en: Conferentia named the state of being gathered together.
items.cn: conferentia 指被聚集到一起的状态。

items.en: French conference named a formal meeting for talks.
items.cn: 法语 conference 指为商谈而举行的正式会面。

items.en: English conference first meant a conversation between parties.
items.cn: 英语 conference 最初指各方之间的交谈。

items.en: It now mainly names a large meeting of people with a shared interest.
items.cn: 如今它主要指有共同兴趣的人举行的大型会议。

note.en: The look-alike group holds nouns built from the same Latin root, and the meaning group names other kinds of gathering.
note.cn: 形近组收的是由同一拉丁词根构成的名词，近义组列出其他类型的聚会。

entries.definition: the act of giving an honour
the giving of a degree or right
the place where two rivers meet
an event where people come together to talk
a large meeting of people with one interest
a small class for discussion and study

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a long table full of microphones, then move to a small closed room and to name badges.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从摆满麦克风的长桌开始，再走到一间关起门的小屋与一排名牌。

normal.en: Confer plus -ence is the noun of bringing people together.
normal.cn: confer 加 -ence，就是把人们聚到一起这件事的名词。

normal.en: A conference is a room where every chair faces the same screen.
normal.cn: 会议就是每把椅子都朝向同一块屏幕的房间。

normal.en: A press conference is a short meeting built for questions.
normal.cn: 记者招待会就是为提问而设的短会。

normal.en: The conference badge tells others which subject you came for.
normal.cn: 会议名牌会告诉别人你是为哪个主题而来。

normal.en: In conference, people confer, and then they return to work.
normal.cn: 在会议里人们商议，然后回到工作中。

abstract.en: Picture a forest of name cards on a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象一长桌上立起一片名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred voices dropping to a whisper.
abstract.cn: 想象上百个声音一起降到耳语。

abstract.en: Picture one slide lighting a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一张幻灯片照亮昏暗的大厅。

examples.en: She gave a talk at the conference on climate.
examples.cn: 她在气候会议上做了报告。

examples.en: The two leaders held a private conference.
examples.cn: 两位领导人举行了私下商谈。

examples.en: Our conference room is booked all morning.
examples.cn: 我们的会议室整个上午都被订满了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conference 记成 confer（带到一起）加 ence：把许多人带到同一个房间，就是会议。

root: 源自拉丁语 conferentia（con 一起 + ferre 携带），本义是聚到一起，后指大型会议与私下协商。

sensesIntro.en: From people carried into one hall, to a few people talking behind a door, and finally to the meeting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被带进同一大厅的人群，到关起门交谈的少数人，最后到会议本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many chairs, one long table, and everyone facing the same subject.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多椅子、一张长桌，所有人都朝向同一个主题。

branches.en: The large meeting is the public and formal side of the word.
branches.cn: 大型会议是这个词公开而正式的一面。

branches.en: The private talk is the same idea behind a closed door.
branches.cn: 私下商谈是同一个意思关起门来的样子。

branches.en: Both sizes of meeting exist to move a subject forward.
branches.cn: 两种规模的会议都为了推动一个议题。

branches.en: A conference is measured by what people carry home from it.
branches.cn: 衡量一场会议，看人们从中带走了什么。

branches.en: A short conference can settle what a long debate cannot.
branches.cn: 一场短商谈有时能解决长辩论解决不了的事。

intro.en: Conference is Latin com-, together, plus ferre, to carry, with the noun ending -ence.
intro.cn: conference 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、ferre（携带）与名词词尾 -ence 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin carry base fer- also appears in transfer and refer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的携带词基 fer- 也出现在 transfer 与 refer 中。

items.example: She attends three conferences a year.

items.exampleCN: 评审团今晚将进行商议。

items.example: The conferment of the medal was brief.
The conferral of rights took years.
items.exampleCN: 这些权利的授予花了好几年。

items.meaning: holding meetings by phone or video
items.example: The team uses video conferencing daily.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队每天使用视频会议。

items.meaning: a meeting held to answer journalists
items.example: The coach called a press conference.
items.exampleCN: 教练召开了一场记者招待会。

items.meaning: to carry across to another place
items.example: Please transfer the call to my office.
items.exampleCN: 请把电话转接到我的办公室。

definition_en: to damage something so badly that it no longer exists or works
core_image: 一堵墙被推倒，砖块和灰一起落到地上
scene: 拆迁队把最后一面墙推倒，灰尘慢慢散开。 The fire destroyed the whole warehouse in an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 destroy 指「摧毁」（第 1 个义项：彻底破坏到无法再用）；句意是那场火在一个小时内烧毁了整座仓库。

senses.title: Break it beyond repair
senses.definition: to damage something so badly that nothing useful is left
senses.definitionCN: 破坏得极其严重，不剩下任何有用的部分
senses.example: The fire destroyed the whole warehouse in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 那场火在一个小时内烧毁了整座仓库。
senses.why: Building takes many hands; undoing needs only one force.
senses.whyCN: 建造需要许多双手，拆掉只需一股力气。

senses.title: End something invisible
senses.definition: to end something such as hope, trust or confidence completely
senses.definitionCN: 把希望、信任或信心之类彻底终结
senses.example: One careless word destroyed her confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不慎的话毁掉了她的信心。
senses.why: A word can knock down a wall nobody can see.
senses.whyCN: 一句话就能推倒一堵谁也看不见的墙。

senses.title: Wipe out living things
senses.definition: to kill an animal or defeat an enemy completely
senses.definitionCN: 把动物杀死或把敌人彻底打败
senses.example: The disease destroyed whole herds that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天，这种病消灭了整群整群的牲畜。
senses.why: The same force that breaks stone can empty a field of animals.
senses.whyCN: 打碎石头的力气，也能让一片田野不再有牲畜。

intro.en: Destroy comes from Latin destruere, to unbuild, built on de-, down, and struere, to pile up or build.
intro.cn: destroy 来自拉丁语 destruere（拆掉建筑），由 de-（向下）与 struere（堆起、建造）构成。

items.en: Struere meant to pile up stones, and de- reversed the piling.
items.cn: struere 指把石头堆起来，前缀 de- 把这堆叠反过来。

items.en: Destruere was used for pulling down walls and for ruining plans.
items.cn: destruere 既用于拆墙，也用于毁掉计划。

items.en: Destruire carried both the physical and the moral sense.
items.cn: destruire 同时带着物质与道义两层意思。

items.en: English destroy covered buildings, armies and reputations.
items.cn: 英语的 destroy 涵盖建筑、军队与名声。

items.en: Today it also names what pollution and fire do to the natural world.
items.cn: 如今它也指污染与大火对自然所做的事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same stem, and the meaning group all leave something in pieces.
note.cn: 形近组共用同一词干，近义组则都把某物弄得支离破碎。

entries.definition: a person or ship that destroys
causing great damage
the act or result of destroying
to spoil something completely
to pull a building down
to damage something badly by force

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a falling wall and end with an empty field where animals used to stand.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一堵倒下的墙开始，落到一片曾经站着牲畜的空地。

normal.en: De- plus struere is un-building: the pile is taken apart.
normal.cn: de- 加 struere 就是拆建：把那堆东西拆开。

normal.en: A builder needs a year; a fire needs an hour.
normal.cn: 建造者要一年，一场火只要一个小时。

normal.en: Words destroy confidence with the same ease as fire destroys wood.
normal.cn: 言语毁掉信心，就像火烧掉木头一样容易。

normal.en: The word can empty a building, a hope or a field.
normal.cn: 这个词能让一栋房子、一份希望或一片田野空掉。

normal.en: Add in- and the wall refuses to fall.
normal.cn: 加上 in-，那堵墙就不肯倒了。

abstract.en: Picture bricks sliding out of a wall one course at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象砖块一层层从墙上滑落。

abstract.en: Picture a letter torn once and then again.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被撕了一次，又被撕了一次。

abstract.en: Picture a fire glowing behind a warehouse window.
abstract.cn: 想象仓库窗后透出一片火光。

examples.en: The fire destroyed the whole warehouse in an hour.
examples.cn: 那场火在一个小时内烧毁了整座仓库。

examples.en: One careless word destroyed her confidence.
examples.cn: 一句不慎的话毁掉了她的信心。

examples.en: The disease destroyed whole herds that winter.
examples.cn: 那年冬天，这种病消灭了整群整群的牲畜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 destroy 记成「地死拖伊」：de 是去掉，stroy 像「堆」，把堆好的东西拖散，就是摧毁。

root: 来自拉丁语 destruere，由 de-（向下、去掉）与 struere（堆起、建造）组成，经古法语 destruire 进入英语。本义是把堆好的建筑拆掉，后来扩展到毁掉希望与名声，也指消灭大批动物或彻底打败敌人。

sensesIntro.en: From a wall taken apart stone by stone, to a confidence broken by a word, to a herd wiped out.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一块块拆掉的墙，到被一句话击碎的信心，再到整群被消灭的牲畜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a built thing coming apart faster than it was built.
core.cn: 核心意象：建起来的东西散得比建时更快。

branches.en: The first sense is the physical pile coming down.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那堆实物塌下来。

branches.en: The second sense is an invisible wall coming down.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一堵看不见的墙塌下来。

branches.en: The third sense is a living population erased.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一群活物被抹去。

branches.en: Bricks and confidence both fall when their supports are removed.
branches.cn: 砖块与信心，在支撑被抽走时都会倒下。

branches.en: Fire, flood and disease all use the same verb.
branches.cn: 火、洪水与疾病，用的都是同一个动词。

intro.en: Destroy gives a large family about pulling down, from the person who does it to the thing that cannot be undone.
intro.cn: destroy 给出一大族表示拆毁的词，从动手的人到无法被拆掉的东西。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin struere, to build, and de- turns building into un-building.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 struere（建造），前缀 de- 把建造变成拆毁。

items.exampleCN: 高温会破坏这种维生素。

items.example: The town was destroyed in a night.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子一夜之间被毁。

items.example: They are destroying the old wall.

items.meaning: one who destroys, or a warship
items.exampleCN: 那艘驱逐舰离开了港口。
这场风暴造成了巨大破坏。
这个箱子好像怎么都弄不坏。

definition_zh: 抓；挠；划痕；从零开始；临时凑的
definition_en: to rub the skin with something sharp, a mark made by scratching, or something started or gathered from nothing
core_image: 猫伸出爪子，在沙发边缘留下几道细细的划痕
scene: 猫在沙发边缘抓了几下。 The cat scratched the edge of the sofa.
sceneCN: 这里 scratch 是「抓；挠」（第 1 个义项）；句意：猫在沙发边缘抓了几下。

senses.title: To rub with something sharp
senses.definition: to rub the skin with nails or a sharp object
senses.definitionCN: 用指甲或尖锐物摩擦皮肤
senses.example: He scratched his head in confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 他困惑地挠了挠头。
senses.why: The core sense is a quick, sharp rubbing motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是快速而尖锐的摩擦动作。

senses.title: A mark from scratching
senses.definition: a thin mark made by something sharp
senses.definitionCN: 由尖锐物造成的细长痕迹
senses.example: The table has a deep scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上有一道很深的划痕。
senses.why: The action leaves a visible line.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作留下可见的线条。

senses.title: From the very beginning
senses.definition: starting with nothing prepared or existing
senses.definitionCN: 从没有任何准备或基础的状态开始
senses.example: She built the site from scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 她白手起家建起了这个网站。
senses.why: Starting from scratch means starting before any mark is made.
senses.whyCN: 从零开始就像在任何痕迹出现之前起步。

senses.title: Gathered in a hurry
senses.definition: made or gathered quickly from whatever is available
senses.definitionCN: 用现有条件匆忙组成或收集的
senses.example: They fielded a scratch team.
senses.exampleCN: 他们临时凑了一支队伍。
senses.why: A scratch group is put together without planning.
senses.whyCN: 临时拼凑的群体没有经过计划。

intro.en: Scratch comes from Middle English scracchen, probably imitating the sound of scratching.
intro.cn: scratch 源自中古英语 scracchen，可能模仿刮擦的声音。

items.en: Scracchen meant to scratch or claw.
items.cn: scracchen 意为抓或挠。

items.en: Scratch named a mark made on a surface.
items.cn: scratch 指留在表面上的痕迹。

items.en: From scratch meant starting at the beginning line.
items.cn: from scratch 意为从起点线开始。

items.en: A scratch team meant one gathered in a hurry.
items.cn: scratch team 指匆忙凑成的队伍。

items.en: Scratch covers clawing, marks, and starting from zero.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scratch 涵盖抓挠、划痕与从零开始。

note.en: Scratch is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs for scraping and clawing.
note.cn: 把 scratch 与形近词以及表示刮擦和抓挠的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to rub a hard edge over a surface
to make something longer
to make a high harsh sound
to scratch with sharp nails
to mark a surface by rubbing
to break the skin lightly

normalIntro.en: Scratch is a quick sharp action that leaves a mark.
normalIntro.cn: scratch 是留下痕迹的快速尖锐动作。

normal.en: A cat scratches with its claws.
normal.cn: 猫用爪子抓。

normal.en: Scratch your head when puzzled.
normal.cn: 困惑时挠挠头。

normal.en: Build from scratch means start with nothing.
normal.cn: from scratch 意为从零开始。

normal.en: Scratch the surface means barely begin.
normal.cn: scratch the surface 意为只触及表面。

normal.en: A scratchy sweater feels rough.
normal.cn: scratchy 的毛衣摸起来刺痒。

abstract.en: A scratch is a memory left on a surface.
abstract.cn: 划痕是留在表面上的记忆。

abstract.en: Starting from scratch means no marks exist yet.

core_image: 一圈高大的树把平静的小湖围在中间
scene: 高高的树围绕着那座小湖。 Tall trees surround the small lake.

senses.title: To be all around
senses.definition: to be placed all around something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物四周
senses.example: Tall trees surround the small lake.

senses.title: To close in on

senses.why: The spatial image extends to atmosphere and circumstance.
senses.whyCN: 空间意象延伸到氛围与境况。
